notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. All app figures reconstructed by reading the fetcher/hook/RPC and evaluating its exact predicates; all true figures recomputed independently in SQL against dev oqermaidggvanahumjmj. Read-only throughout — no writes, no DDL, prod never touched. Reference date 2026-08-05; headline comparisons at scope preset "All" (2000-01-01 → 2100-01-01) because "This Month" on dev is 6 bookings and 5 invoices and would not support a conclusion.

WHAT THE PASS FOUND. Seven of the eight financial surfaces are wrong, and the wrongness is invisible by construction — no toast, no error boundary, no failed request, no "N rows excluded" note anywhere. Five distinct root causes, all upstream of the arithmetic:

1. THREE COLUMNS THE CODE READS DO NOT EXIST. invoices has no remaining_balance and no payment_status; billing_line_items has no total_amount; invoices has no invoice_type and no reversal_for. Confirmed against information_schema and, for the PostgREST paths, against the live REST endpoint (HTTP 400, 42703). Two consequences: baseRemainingBalance() silently returns the full invoice amount so Booking Cash Flow's "Outstanding AR" can never fall below "Total Invoiced"; and the entire Unbilled Revenue Report 400s and renders PHP 0.00 with the words "No unbilled bookings this period." while PHP 2,803,905.99 sits unbilled. Reading `data.total_amount` off an object that never had the key returns undefined, not an error — that is why this survived.

2. A PHANTOM STATUS ALLOWLIST, IN SIX PLACES. ['approved','posted','paid','partial'] — three of those four match zero e-voucher rows on dev. What is missing is 'disbursed': PHP 350,307.25 of booking-linked expense where the cash has physically left the company. Cost of sales is understated 50.4% and gross profit overstated by the identical amount. The DB-layer .in() is also case-sensitive, so the legacy 'Approved' row is dropped before the client-side lowercasing can save it. Note the code comments at dashboardFetchers.ts:144-147 show someone already found and fixed this class of bug for quotations — the same audit was never run against e-vouchers.

3. AN INVOICE STATUS ALLOWLIST THAT OMITS 'Issued'. PHP 485,000.00 — 77.5% of billings, 98.5% of AR — classified as financially inactive and dropped from three reports. The single fallback that would have caught it tests payment_status, a column that does not exist.

4. A JOIN ON A COLUMN THAT HOLDS THE WRONG KIND OF IDENTIFIER. get_financial_health_summary joins billing_line_items.project_number → projects.project_number. 83 of 88 non-empty values are BOOKING numbers (the known L3 shape). 5 of 88 join. Financial Health reports PHP 125,000.00 of billings against PHP 2,967,027.59 actual, PHP 0.00 of expenses against PHP 801,050.25 actual, and a 100.0% gross margin for a freight forwarder.

5. PERIOD LOGIC. The DB session TimeZone is UTC (verified) while FinancialHealthPage builds its 'YYYY-MM' from the browser's local Manila clock — an 8-hour disagreement window every day at every month boundary. Receivables Aging scopes by invoice created_at, which makes its own 61-90 and 91+ buckets structurally unreachable under any month scope. And both booking-financials hooks fetch collections with .gte(fromIso) and no upper bound, so post-period cash reduces in-period outstanding.

TWO REAL MATCHES, REPORTED AS RESULTS. Collections Report agrees to the centavo (PHP 133,621.60 / 7 receipts / avg 19,088.80 / largest 25,000.00) and correctly excludes the one 'credited' receipt — though on 7 rows of single-currency data that is a pass rather than a proof. Booking Cash Flow's "Total Booked Charges" also agrees exactly at PHP 2,945,027.59 given its own definition; the problem there is the label, not the sum.

THE MOST DANGEROUS ONE. If only one thing gets fixed first, make it the Unbilled Revenue Report. Every other figure here is wrong by a margin; that one is a fully-formatted, signature-blocked document asserting PHP 0.00 against a PHP 2.8M reality, and its empty state is worded as reassurance. A manager who opens it learns something false and has no signal at all that anything failed.

CROSS-REPORT INCONSISTENCY WORTH FLAGGING SEPARATELY. Sales Report and Booking Cash Flow both display "Outstanding AR" on the same dataset and disagree by PHP 133,621.60 (7,500.00 vs 141,121.60) — the Sales Report derives it as billed−collected, Booking Cash Flow via the dead remaining_balance path. Likewise "Open Inquiries" means 128 rows on the BD dashboard and 58 on the Executive dashboard. Two screens, one word, different numbers, no footnote.

FOLLOW-UP I COULD NOT COMPLETE ON DEV. The FX/base_amount paths are entirely unexercised (all dev rows are PHP) yet two aggregates — useUnbilledRevenueReport and the whole Financial Health RPC — demonstrably sum raw amount rather than base_amount. The 4 'Issued' invoices are kpi-sim-* fixture rows, so the PHP 485,000 is seeded data. The defect — a hardcoded seven-word status allow-list, plus a fallback reading a column that does not exist — is real regardless of whose rows tripped it.
notes:
Scope of the pass: every figure rendered by src/components/accounting/FinancialsModule.tsx (4 KPI strips = 16 cards, 1 aging strip = 5 buckets, 4 grouped tables and their subtotals), recomputed independently in SQL against dev (oqermaidggvanahumjmj). Read-only throughout; no writes, no prod contact. "Today" for all aging arithmetic is 2026-08-05 and the default landing scope is This Month = August 2026.

The good news, stated plainly because a match is a result: the arithmetic inside this file is almost entirely correct. Every KPI total equals the sum of the rows beneath it. The aging strip sums to the Outstanding KPI to the centavo (PHP 43,500.00). calculateInvoiceBalance is right on both invoices I recomputed by hand, correctly excludes 'credited' collections, and correctly avoids double-counting a collection that carries both invoice_id and a linked_billings entry pointing at the same invoice. The file's headline claim — that invoices.status is a document lifecycle and settlement must come from collections — is true, and every figure on the invoices tab does route through settlementOf/calculateInvoiceBalance rather than status. And the month boundary is handled correctly for Manila: a row at 2026-08-01T00:30+08:00 is placed in August, because getDateScopeQueryRange builds the range from local midnight and .toISOString()s it while isInScope compares local calendar days.

So the failures here are not arithmetic failures. They are input failures — the numbers are computed correctly over the wrong set of rows, and there is nothing on the screen that could tell you.

Three are severe enough to act on before anything else:

1. applyScope filters on columns that do not exist. billing_line_items has neither created_by nor assigned_to; the other three tables have created_by but no assigned_to. Confirmed live: HTTP 400 / 42703 from dev PostgREST. The queryFn swallows the error into an empty array, so 42 of 60 dev users see a fully-rendered Financials module reporting PHP 0.00 everywhere, with no error and no empty state. useDataScope's fail-closed default is {type:'own'}, so this is also what a brand-new user gets.

2. settlementOf computes balances against the DATE-SCOPED collections, not all of them. Narrow the scope to a window that cuts between an invoice and its payment and the invoice reappears as unpaid and overdue. Demonstrable on real dev data: a Jul 1–17 range shows BR202606-126-001 as OVERDUE PHP 8,000.00, an invoice that was settled in full on Jul 18. Outstanding and Overdue are wrong by construction for every scope narrower than "all".

3. Two status vocabularies are simply wrong. isInvoiceVisibleDocument's seven-word allow-list deletes 4 invoices worth PHP 485,000 from every total in every scope (and its payment_status fallback reads a column the invoices table does not have). The Expenses "Pending Approval" KPI tests for a literal 'pending' that no e-voucher has ever carried, so it reads 0 / "all clear" while PHP 3,684,843.57 across 227 vouchers sits in an approval queue.

Below that sits a cluster of dead field mappings in the evoucher→expense mapper (expense_category, category, request_date, expense_date, voucher_number, total_amount — six reads, six non-existent columns), which is why Top Category is permanently "General"; the same class of defect gives the Collections tab a permanently blank Invoice # column and a permanently "N/A" Avg Days to Collect.

Suggested order of work: (a) fix applyScope — drop assigned_to, and skip owner-filtering billing_line_items entirely since it has no owner column, letting RLS do the cut; (b) surface fetch errors instead of coercing them to [] — a failed query must never render as PHP 0.00; (c) fetch collections unscoped for settlement; (d) replace both hardcoded status allow-lists with the live vocabulary; (e) exclude drafts from Outstanding/Overdue, and split the Expenses total into requested vs disbursed.

thinEvidence: THE HEADLINE CAVEAT: dev contains ZERO non-PHP rows. Every one of 15 invoices, 8 collections, 267 e-vouchers, 175 billing line items and 315 quotations is currency='PHP'. Every stored exchange_rate is either 1.00000000 or NULL. Therefore NO multi-currency arithmetic was exercised by data — every FX finding below is read from the code path, not observed in a row, and every 'agrees' on an FX-consistency check is agreement on the degenerate case rate=1. Multi-currency in this product is untested, not working.

The `exchange_rates` table holds exactly ONE row: USD→PHP 58.00000000, rate_date 2026-05-03, source 'manual', notes 'Seed rate for dev/staging'. As of 2026-08-05 that is 94 days stale, and resolveExchangeRate() returns it with fromTable:true and no staleness check.

136 of 175 billing_line_items have base_amount NULL and exchange_rate NULL (the pre-FX-migration rows). 4 of 15 invoices and 1 of 267 e-vouchers likewise. All are PHP so pickReportingAmount's fallback to raw amount is currently harmless — but it means 78% of billing rows have no FX metadata to check against, so the 'zero inconsistencies' result covers only 39 rows.

0 rows anywhere have currency <> 'PHP'. The specific check asked for — rows where currency is foreign but exchange_rate is 1 or NULL or base_amount = amount — returns 0 because the population is 0, not because the writers prevent it. Two writers (send_billing_items_to_booking, ensure_billable_expense_billing_item) provably CREATE exactly that shape, and one client path (InvoiceBuilder) provably ships it.
The `expenses` table has 0 rows and is not read by the financial dashboard at all — expenses are mapped from `evouchers`. Any conclusion about 'expense' figures is a conclusion about e-vouchers.

The cross-currency collection case (a receipt in one currency against an invoice in another) could not be exercised: 8 collections, all PHP, 7 of them one-to-one against a single PHP invoice. The ±0.05 reconciliation guard at CollectionCreatorPanel.tsx:411-420 reads as correct on inspection and I could not make it fire.
The roundMoney drift result is a synthetic sweep (800,000 amount×rate combinations against exact integer-scaled arithmetic), not observed data — no posting on dev uses a fractional rate.

'0 discrepancies across 264 e-voucher header-vs-line reconciliations' is a real result and the largest sample in this pass, but it tests only that a single-currency sum adds up. evoucher_line_items has no currency column at all, so a foreign-currency voucher's lines carry bare numbers whose currency lives only on the header.
notes:
METHOD. I read each figure's fetcher/reducer, wrote down what it computes rather than what it is labelled, then recomputed from source rows in SQL without reusing the app's query. Where the numbers agree I say so; where the population is empty I say the check was vacuous rather than passed.

THE ONE SENTENCE. The arithmetic on this data is right almost everywhere — and that is not reassuring, because the data is 100% PHP at rate 1, which is the one case where every wrong formula produces the right answer.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN TODAY, IN PHP, WITH NO FX INVOLVED:
The same receivable is PHP 651,500.00 on the Financials dashboard and PHP 528,500.00 one tab across. The gap is exactly one voided invoice, BR202606-121-001, PHP 123,000.00. FinancialsModule.tsx:719-732 wraps the shared helper in a status check; FinancialDashboard.tsx:203-213 calls the helper raw. calculateInvoiceBalance itself has no concept of a dead document — the guard lives in one caller, so every other caller inherits the bug. Two more callers do: the aging strip on the dashboard, and the Attention panel (which additionally reads .balance, the invoice-currency field, instead of .balanceBase). Add the two draft invoices and PHP 36,000 more is receivable that nobody has been asked to pay.

THE FX ARCHITECTURE IS GENUINELY WELL DESIGNED AND ONLY PARTLY WIRED IN.
accountingCurrency.ts is careful: toBaseAmount and resolvePostingRate both throw rather than default a foreign posting to 1, and the comment says so explicitly. exchangeRates.ts is careful too — resolveExchangeRate throws when no rate is on file. The e-voucher panel and the collection panel both use them properly, seed from the table, and the collection panel adds a ±0.05 PHP reconciliation guard that is the single best piece of money code I read in this pass.

Then three paths route around all of it.
1. InvoiceBuilder never imports exchangeRates at all. exchangeRate is useState(1). resolvePostingRate('USD', 1) returns 1 — it only rejects zero and non-finite — so the guard designed to stop exactly this waves it through. Pick USD in the dropdown, do not touch the rate box, save: a USD 10,000 invoice with base_amount 10,000.00 instead of 580,000.00, and base_amount is the field every aggregate trusts.
2. send_billing_items_to_booking() COALESCEs a missing rate to 1 in SQL. The client calling it refuses first (UnifiedBillingsTab.tsx:770-814 — a real, correct guard), but the RPC is SECURITY DEFINER and callable directly by four departments. Guard in the form, not in the writer.
3. FinancialsModule.tsx:325-340 maps e-vouchers to expenses and drops base_amount and exchange_rate on the floor, keeping the currency code beside a raw foreign amount. pickReportingAmount then does exactly what its fallback chain says and returns the unconverted number. That mapper feeds Total Expenses, Net Profit, profit margin, the expenses KPI strip and SalesReport's cost of sales. The same file also reads four columns that do not exist on evouchers (request_date, expense_date, total_amount, voucher_number/expense_name, expense_category) — which is why every expense is dated by keystroke and categorised 'General'.

THE FX GAIN/LOSS MECHANISM DOES NOT EXIST. Four account codes are declared with a comment describing realized-on-settlement and unrealized-at-period-end posting. Grep finds them in the declaring file and its unit test, nowhere else. Disbursement carries the creation-time rate forward and there is no disbursement_exchange_rate column to carry anything else. A USD advance locked at 58 and paid at 60 loses PHP 2 per dollar into no account.

ON THE MANILA/UTC QUESTION you flagged: isInScope (aggregate/types.ts:67-74) normalises with local-time getters, so on a Manila browser it is correct — dates are stored as midnight UTC, which is 08:00 Manila, same day. It breaks for a browser west of UTC, and PLTrendCard's month keys ('2026-08' parsed by new Date) shift a full month there. Not the eight-hours-a-day-wrong shape you predicted; a whose-laptop shape instead. I did not pursue it further since the surface is currency.

A GOOD-NEWS ITEM WORTH THE SAME WEIGHT AS THE BUGS. UnifiedBillingsTab has a genuine pre-save FX guard that names the offending rows, refuses, and explains why in the code comment ('We do NOT fall back to the raw foreign amount for missing rates — that would silently poison PHP aggregates'). Somebody understood this problem exactly. The finding is that they fixed it in one file and the other three paths never learned.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS PASS CONCLUSIVE. Seed dev with a handful of USD documents — one invoice, one collection against it, one e-voucher, one billing line — at a rate other than 1, and re-run this. Until then the correct statement is that multi-currency is unexercised, and that the code paths I read say it would not survive first contact.

Only 1 person (Sarah Baylon) has coverage above 50% in any period, so "Company Median 61.2" and "Below Satisfactory 1 / 1" are single-observation figures. The Performance page's distribution charts, band composition and systemic detection have effectively no data to work on: `rated.length < 3` suppresses every systemic check.
user_targets has exactly 1 row org-wide. Everything about kpi_metric_sales_quota beyond its SQL is inference, and the observed 120% is a seeded fixture.
Financial Health returns 5 rows. "0 discrepancies across 5 rows" for the per-project arithmetic is not evidence the aggregation is right — it is evidence that 170 of 175 rows never reached it.

Currency is PHP on 100% of rows in billing_line_items (175), evouchers (267), invoices (15), collections (8) and quotations (315). The mixed-currency risk in kpi_metric_sales_quota and in the financial RPC is therefore structural and unexercised — I could not produce a wrong number from it on dev.

Only 30 evoucher_line_items carry a kpi_charge_class at all, across 9 catalog items, and none fall in July 2026. The June behaviour I verified (guard correctly returning "awaiting fault review") comes from 6 people.

No kpi_period has status='locked'. The entire snapshot path in get_kpi_scorecard (`IF v_period.status = 'locked' AND v_stored.id IS NOT NULL`) is unexercised, which also means every historical score in the trend chart is recomputed live and can change retroactively.

notes:
METHOD. Every RPC body was read from pg_proc, the formula written down, then recomputed with independent SQL that does not reuse the app's joins. All work was read-only against dev (oqermaidggvanahumjmj). Nothing was written. supabase-prod was not touched.

WHAT MATCHED — and it is worth saying plainly. The scorecard's core arithmetic is sound. I recomputed two full scorecards by hand (Sarah Baylon, 2026-06 and 2026-07) and both agree to the decimal: weighted = weight × rating / 5, score = Σweighted / Σincluded-weight × 100, giving 70.0 and 61.2. Every scorecard_key's definitions sum to exactly 100, so `scored_on_pct` really is a percentage. The exclusion model is honest — excluded KPIs are left out rather than counted as zero, and the denominator shrinks with them. get_kpi_org_overview's provisional flag uses `->>` not `->` (there is a comment in the function about the bug that caused), and its defaults (50/60) match the client's hardcoded PROVISIONAL_COVERAGE_PCT. get_kpi_score_history returns the right three periods in the right order. Quotation TAT recomputed independently from activity_log gives exactly 8 of 10. And in June, where charge lines actually exist, kpi_metric_charge_class correctly refuses to score and says "1 awaiting fault review · 4 on blended catalog items". The engine is well built. What is wrong is almost entirely at the edges where it meets missing data.

THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM. Two failures repeat across both surfaces and account for nearly every finding.

(1) An empty result set is scored instead of excluded. Zero-incident KPIs return 0 for "no rows matched you" and are rewarded with a 5; rate KPIs return 0 for the same condition and are punished with a 1. That single asymmetry produces 33 people at exactly 100.0 "Outstanding" and 5 at exactly 20.0 "Poor" in the same month, from the same underlying fact — that nothing was recorded. The provisional flag mutes the colour but not the number, and both RPCs still emit band='Outstanding'.

(2) A join to a column that does not contain what its name says. Finding L3 is not a naming annoyance — it is the reason the Financial Health report shows ₱125,000 of billings against ₱2,967,027.59 live, and ₱0.00 of expenses against ₱4,534,208.82. That report's headline is a 100% gross margin, rendered in green with an upward arrow. It is the single most dangerous number in this surface: it has no error, it looks like good news, and it is off by the entire cost base.

TWO THINGS THAT EXIST BUT ARE NOT WIRED. kpi_propose_fault and tag_charge_fault are complete, permissioned, SECURITY DEFINER functions that nothing in src/ ever calls — ReviewPanel.tsx:50 filters to source 'logged'|'judgment' and so never shows the `proposed` charge KPIs. Consequently the "awaiting fault review" state can never be cleared through the product, and 30 points of the brokerage card oscillate between permanently-excluded and unearned-5. Conversely, 15 of 42 kpi_definitions name a metric_key with no resolver function; kpi-bdd-meetings is source='auto' with no function, which means no machine computes it and save_kpi_manual_entry refuses to let a human type it — 13 of BDD's 100 points are permanently unreachable by any route.

ONE SMALLER TRUST ITEM worth fixing cheaply: ReviewPanel.tsx:74 sends `p_override_reason: d.reason ?? k.override_reason ?? null`. Change a rating from 4 to 1 without typing a new reason and the server's "a differing rating needs a reason" guard is satisfied by the justification written for the previous, different decision.
